title: Automated, Radiation-Free Detection of Cochlear Implant Electrode Array Migration Using Routine Impedance Telemetry.
summary: A random-forest model used routine impedance telemetry to detect cochlear implant electrode-array migration against radiological reference findings in a retrospective clinical study. The result is a study-specific detection evaluation; it does not establish that radiation can be safely omitted in clinical care.
ai_technology: Random-forest classifier using cochlear implant impedance telemetry
organization: Not stated in the abstract reviewed

evidence.tested: The retrospective cohort compared model classifications with radiological ground truth to evaluate migration detection.
evidence.unknown: Retrospective evidence does not establish prospective workflow performance or safe replacement of radiological assessment.
